a note from the shop

Hi, I'm Michelle.

Purple Moon has been my little corner of the web since 1996. I make a lot of the silver myself, and the rest comes from Grateful Dead tour family artists. The stickers and patches are a collection decades in the making, including vintage designs that are long out of print.

My favorite story: a customer sold her house, and the new owners wouldn't let her take the front door with her baby bear rose sticker on it. She found a replacement here. That's what this shop is for.

~ Michelle & Sunny

Good questions

What's the difference between inside and outside window stickers?

Outside window stickers are sticky on the back and go on almost any smooth surface. Inside window stickers are sticky on the front, so they face out through the glass, which is great where ice scrapers would ruin a sticker. Two-sided stickers have art on both sides and glow like stained glass on a window. Every sticker is waterproof.

Are the jewelry photos the actual size?

Photos are not to scale, so please check the measurements and weight listed on each piece. Many pieces are one of a kind, so the photo is the piece you'll get. Any questions about sizing or stones, just ask!

Do you ship outside the USA?

Yes, anywhere in the world: $4.00 up to $35, $15.00 up to $75, $25.00 up to $125, $35.00 up to $175 and $40.00 over $175. Orders over $35 include insurance. Smaller international orders go First Class Air Mail without tracking unless you ask for Registered Mail.

How can I pay?

PayPal at checkout, or by personal check or money order. Email me and I'll send the details.

What does "gone but not forgotten" mean?

When I sell out of something I can't replace, it moves to the sold archive. Older designs do get reprinted now and then, and vintage ones turn up in the strangest places, so if you're hunting for one, ask.

Ordering & paying

How can I pay?

Check out with PayPal, or pay by personal check or money order. If you’d like to mail a payment, and I’ll send the details.

Are the jewelry photos the actual size?

Photos are not to scale, so check the measurements on each listing. Many pieces are one of a kind, so the photo is the piece you’ll get.

What is the jewelry made of?

Each listing says. The Grateful Dead and solid sterling pieces are .925 sterling silver, most with natural stones. Some peace and pride pieces are pewter, stainless steel, leather or hemp, and the dichroic glass is handmade kiln-fired glass.

Why do dichroic glass pieces look different in person?

The colors shimmer and shift as the light moves, which makes them very hard to photograph. Every piece is one of a kind and looks even better in person. A black satin cord is free if you ask for one at checkout.

Do you have pieces that aren’t on the site?

Often! New pieces show up before they’re photographed, and I’m always hunting for old stickers. If you’re looking for something in particular, .

Shipping

How do you ship?

Orders in the USA go by USPS First Class with tracking and insurance. Stickers are wrapped in plastic, backed with recycled cardboard and sealed in a manila envelope. A few recycled packing peanuts turn the envelope into a package, which is what lets it be tracked. Priority and Express Mail are options at checkout.

How much is shipping in the USA?

It’s based on the merchandise total: $3.49 up to $30, $5.49 up to $50, $7.99 up to $100, $11.99 up to $200, and $15.99 over $200.

Do you ship outside the USA?

Yes, anywhere in the world: $4.00 up to $35, $15.00 up to $75, $25.00 up to $125, $35.00 up to $175 and $40.00 over $175. Orders under $35 go by First Class Air Mail without tracking or insurance. Orders from $35 to $75 go by Registered Mail and orders over $75 by Priority Mail International, both insured. Want insurance on a smaller order? Ask about adding Registered Mail.

Stickers

Why stickers?

Stickers are art anyone can own. Lots of talented artists have made work just for stickers, and they’re small enough to go anywhere. People get attached to them, too: one customer framed his whole collection of VW stickers and hung it on the wall.

Where do all these stickers come from?

I’ve been collecting and selling stickers for almost 30 years. It started on Grateful Dead tour, where artists pushed sticker art to new heights. Every sticker here is an original, professionally printed one, either mint condition vintage or brand new. Vintage designs are out of print, so quantities are limited. Have vintage stickers to sell? I’d love to hear from you. And the collection will always stay family friendly and hate-free.

Are they weatherproof? Where can they go?

All of them are waterproof. On a clean, dry surface they’ll stick to cars, campers, bikes, boats, snowboards, coolers, lockers, toolboxes, windows, walls, shower doors and just about anywhere else you can think of. No paper stickers or home printouts here.

What’s the difference between a sticker and a decal?

Honestly, nobody agrees! Ask ten sticker vendors and you’ll get ten answers. I call anything flat and sticky a sticker, but decal works too.

Outside window stickers

Clear around the edges and see-through in the art, so light comes through. Printed on one side with the sticky part on the back, and they go on almost any smooth surface.

Inside window stickers

Same look, but the sticky part is on the front, so they go on the inside of the glass facing out. Great if you live where it snows, since an ice scraper can’t reach them.

Two-sided window stickers

Art on both sides, so they look just as good from inside as out, a lot like stained glass. They can go on either side of the window. One thing to know: if a two-sided outside sticker with words goes on the inside of the glass, the words will read backwards from outside.

Vinyl stickers

Solid, so no light comes through, with art on the front and sticky on the back. Bumper stickers are vinyl, and so is mylar, the extra thick glossy kind. Very tough and they stick to any smooth surface.

Static cling stickers

Flexible plastic with no glue at all, so they peel off and go back on again and again. If one stops clinging, rinse it gently in warm water and pat it dry with a lint-free cloth.

Rub-on transfers

Bold, usually one-color designs cut from tough vinyl, with no background at all, so they look painted on. Great for windows, cars, surfboards, skateboards and guitars, and they’re waterproof once they’re on.

Putting stickers on (and taking them off)

How do I put on a window sticker?
  1. Clean the glass with window cleaner and let it dry.
  2. Grab a credit card or another plastic straight edge (not metal).
  3. Peel back a corner of the backing. On a big sticker, only peel about half to start.
  4. Line up one edge, then smooth the sticker down with the card as you go, pushing air bubbles out toward the edges.
  5. Peel the rest of the backing and finish smoothing from the center out.
  6. Still have a bubble? Poke a tiny hole in it with a pin and smooth the air out through the hole.
How do I put on a rub-on transfer?
  1. Clean the spot with glass cleaner or rubbing alcohol.
  2. Peel off the top paper. The design comes with it, and that side is very sticky.
  3. Place it sticky side down and rub over the paper with a spoon, card, coin or fingernail, getting every fine line.
  4. Slowly peel the paper away. If part of the design lifts, lay it back down and rub again.
How do I take a sticker off?

On glass, a razor blade scrapes it right off. On most other surfaces, hot soapy water and a kitchen scrubbie take care of leftover sticky stuff. Some people swear by Goo Gone.

The sold archive

What does “gone but not forgotten” mean?

Some designs, like dancing bears and classic stealies, are still being printed. Others had a limited run. When I sell out of something I can’t replace, it moves to the .

Will sold pieces ever come back?

I’ve learned never to say never. Old designs get reprinted now and then, and vintage stickers turn up in the strangest places. If you’re hunting for one, and I’ll keep an eye out.
